name: The Barkley Marathons
one_line: A race born from a failed prison escape, where 63 percent of editions end with nobody finishing - and the first woman to survive it did so with 99 seconds to spare.

facts.claim: in 1977 a convict escaped Brushy Mountain penitentiary into the Tennessee mountains and was caught having covered about 8 miles in 54 hours; local runner Gary Cantrell scoffed that he could do at least 100 - and created the race
facts.note: Cantrell verbatim: 'I could do at least 100 miles.' The escapee was James Earl Ray - state plainly if used; the fact is historical. Race founded 1986, named for Cantrell's neighbor Barry Barkley. Cantrell goes by 'Lazarus Lake'.

facts.claim: entry costs $1.60, requires an essay titled 'Why I Should Be Allowed to Run in the Barkley', and first-timers must bring a license plate
facts.note: The plates hang at camp (we have the photo). Each year one strong runner is invited as the 'sacrificial virgin' - picked because Cantrell believes they will fail.

facts.claim: five loops of unmarked mountain terrain, officially 100 miles - closer to 130 in practice - with roughly 60,000 feet of climb and a 60-hour limit
facts.note: 60,000 ft is about twice Everest from sea level. Two water stations, no other aid. Course changes yearly.

facts.claim: runners prove their route by finding hidden books and tearing out the page matching their bib number
the race begins when Lazarus Lake lights a cigarette; a conch blast an hour earlier is the only warning
facts.note: Wikipedia verbatim: 'the race officially begins when Cantrell lights a cigarette.' We have the photo.

facts.claim: in the race's four-decade history there have been 26 finishes by only 20 people; about 63 percent of editions end with no finisher at all
facts.note: As of 2026. Nearly 800 had attempted by 2013 with 12 finishers at that point.

facts.claim: in 2024 Jasmin Paris became the first woman ever to finish, collapsing at the gate in 59:58:21 - 99 seconds inside the 60-hour cutoff
facts.note: Confirmed by CNN/ESPN/iRunFar. Part two of our Jasmin Paris video - she is this video's climax; the race is its subject.

comparison.gap_description: 59:58:21 against a 60:00:00 wall - 99 seconds of margin after roughly 130 miles.

story_beat: In 2024, the sixty-hour clock nearly gone, Jasmin Paris - a veterinary lecturer and mother of two - sprinted the final climb and collapsed against the yellow gate with 99 seconds to spare: the first woman to finish in the race's history.

image_cues.query: !Sharpshooter at Brushy Mountain State Prison naps after esc
